main_body: A blue-grey metal/sci-fi wall panel face with an orange trim band near the top, vertical panel seams, rivets, orange shelf-like bars, a vent grille, and a dark lower kick plate.
top_band: none; the column from the top shows a light blue-grey cap line (rows 0-1), a dark strip, blue-grey wall with an orange band (rows 5-6), then the panel face. No horizontal surface is visible from above.
evidence: The kind is terrain (wall face), so a flat front view is expected for a wall tile. Judged strictly against the contract, though, it is a pure front elevation: panels, seams, vent and bars are all vertical-face details, with only 1-2px lines marking ledges, and no top surface is drawn. Fails the 3/4 check.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 3 lightness steps on its blue-grey ramp: a light edge, a mid fill and a dark seam. Large panel areas (e.g. 10x10 px) are a single flat colour with only sparse rivet dots, and there is no grain or speckle. The orange bars are 2-3 tone flat strips. The Beodeul timber and stone references carry per-stone shading, plaster speckle and wood grain, so each of their tiles holds many more colours. The dark seams and lines are bluish-dark and mostly near-black, so the outline reads mixed. This is plainly thinner and flatter than the reference.
